title: Flow control and shared media
subtitle: How a sender keeps the wire busy without drowning the receiver, recovers from loss, and shares a cable with others.

sections.title: Stop-and-wait
sections.body: In ARQ (automatic repeat request) the receiver acknowledges good frames and the sender retransmits after a timeout. Stop-and-wait sends one frame, waits for its ACK, then sends the next. It is correct and trivial, but the link sits idle for a whole round trip per frame: with a long pipe the utilisation is tiny.

worked.why: 1 Mb/s link, 1000-bit frames, one-way delay 20 ms.
Frame time 1 ms; round trip 40 ms. Utilisation = frame time / (frame time + RTT).

questions.prompt: Why is stop-and-wait poor on a long fast link?

choices.text: The sender idles for a whole round trip after each frame.

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: Bandwidth × delay bits could be in flight but only one frame is.

figures.caption: Figure 3.6.1 — stop-and-wait
figures.note: Four frames take 16 time units: each waits for its own acknowledgement.

sections.title: Sliding window: Go-Back-N and Selective Repeat
sections.body: A sliding window lets the sender have up to W unacknowledged frames in flight. Go-Back-N: the receiver accepts only the next expected frame, so one loss forces the sender to resend that frame and all after it. Selective Repeat: the receiver buffers out-of-order frames and acknowledges each, so only the lost frame is resent. With window 4 and frame 2 lost: Go-Back-N retransmits 4 frames, Selective Repeat just 1.

questions.prompt: Why does Go-Back-N resend frames that arrived safely?

choices.text: The receiver discarded them: it accepts frames only in order.
The ACKs for them were lost.

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: That keeps the receiver trivial — no buffer — at the cost of extra traffic.

figures.caption: Figure 3.7.1 — Go-Back-N
figures.note: Go-Back-N: after the loss the whole window is resent.

problems.prompt: A 1 Mb/s link, 1000-bit frames, RTT 40 ms. What window size keeps the link fully busy?
problems.answer: Frame time 1 ms; RTT 40 ms. Window ≥ 1 + 40/1 = 41 frames.

sections.title: Random access: ALOHA and CSMA
sections.body: When many stations share a medium, collisions happen. Pure ALOHA: transmit whenever you like — maximum throughput 18.4% (1/2e). Slotted ALOHA: transmit only at slot starts — 36.8% (1/e). CSMA listens first; CSMA/CD (Ethernet) also listens while sending and aborts on a collision, then waits a random back-off that doubles each time; CSMA/CA (Wi-Fi) cannot hear collisions, so it avoids them with random waits and acknowledgements.

worked.why: Pure ALOHA throughput S = G·e^(−2G) peaks at G = 0.5.
Slotted ALOHA S = G·e^(−G) peaks at G = 1.

questions.prompt: Why can Wi-Fi not use collision detection?

choices.text: A station cannot hear other transmissions while it is sending on the same radio channel.

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: So it avoids collisions (CSMA/CA) rather than detecting them.

sections.title: Switched Ethernet and VLANs
sections.body: A switch gives every port its own collision domain, so modern Ethernet is full duplex and needs no CSMA/CD. A VLAN splits one physical switch into several logical LANs; frames carry an 802.1Q tag with a VLAN id, and only a router moves traffic between VLANs. Uses: isolate departments, limit broadcasts, apply security.

sections.title: Efficiency of the window
sections.body: Link utilisation with a window of W frames is U = W × tframe / (tframe + RTT), capped at 1. The product bandwidth × delay tells you how many bits are needed in flight to fill the pipe; choose W at least that many frames.

worked.why: 100 Mb/s link, 1250-byte frames (10 000 bits), RTT 10 ms.
Frame time = 10 000 / 10⁸ = 0.1 ms; RTT / frame time = 100.
Window needed to fill the pipe: 1 + 100 = 101 frames. With W = 7, utilisation is only 7 / 101.

questions.prompt: What does bandwidth × delay tell you?

choices.text: How many bits must be in flight to keep the link busy.

sections.title: Summary
sections.body:
• Sliding windows keep the pipe full; window ≥ 1 + RTT/frame-time.
  • GBN resends the window; SR resends only the lost frame.
  • CSMA/CD detects, CSMA/CA avoids.
